summary.headline: Route Mobile Q1 FY27 revenue rose 9.6% YoY to INR 11,515 mn, but adjusted EBITDA margin fell to 9.5% and gross margin to 20.9%.
summary.overview: Revenue from operations returned to YoY growth, up 9.6% YoY and 1.8% QoQ, with new products (RCS, WhatsApp, other IP messaging) growing 14% YoY and 11% QoQ. Gross margin fell to 20.9% from 23.3% in Q4 FY26, driven mainly by temporary traffic disruption at one large high-margin Indian customer during a product deployment, plus a security incident at the Colombian subsidiary and aggregator margin pressure. Adjusted EBITDA was INR 1,089 mn (down 18.9% QoQ), and adjusted PAT was INR 686 mn (up 16.6% YoY). Management announced the slump-sale acquisition of Heltar Technologies' business undertaking (signed July 13, closing in weeks), and said FY27 guidance is being held for now.

financial_highlights.change: vs 21.4% in Q1 FY26 and 23.3% in Q4 FY26
Driven by salary inflation, consulting fees and a provision for an advance

financial_highlights.value: Approx. 8-9% of revenue (per analyst; not stated by management)

segments.name: New products (RCS, WhatsApp, other IP messaging)
segments.commentary: Revenue grew 14% YoY and 11% QoQ, ahead of company average; management calls it the engine of business mix transformation. Non-SMS revenue has compounded over 40% annually for four years per management.

segments.name: Domestic SMS
segments.commentary: Traction described as good, except for the specific large Indian customer where traffic was disrupted; India entity segment profit turned negative this quarter.

segments.name: ILD (international long distance)
segments.commentary: Growth lagging company average but not declining per management; still significant given large global customers and large ticket sizes. Management did not disclose ILD/NLD split.

guidance_outlook: FY27 guidance (revenue, margin, dividend) held for now; management expects to revisit in future quarters, saying it is 'on track' with dividend.
Management said it should not materially deviate from the adjusted EBITDA margin guidance (about 12% per analyst reference), with clarity by end of Q2; some items may be stickier.
Volumes expected to grow 10-15% in the next couple of quarters as the season sets in.
Gross margin could land in a 21.5%-23% range over coming quarters, the band of the last 5-6 quarters, depending on recovery; no commitment on margin expansion or dilution from non-SMS mix in FY27.
Operating cash conversion (EBITDA to CFO) expected to return to 75%-100% for the rest of the year; management is comfortable with ~75% for full year.
Salary cost expected to be flat from here; headcount around 800, with backfills and selective hiring.
Heltar contribution expected to ramp gradually, with scaling more visible by end of FY27 rather than Q2.
capex_capacity: Heltar acquisition: slump sale of identified business undertaking (brand, IP, technology platform, team) signed July 13, 2026; closing expected in coming weeks, funded from internal accruals and described as not material to the balance sheet.
Claro multi-country firewall deal: deployment is behind schedule; management hopes to go live this quarter, with tangible revenue to follow; deal is fixed plus variable.
Masivian (Colombia subsidiary) security incident: investigation ongoing; platform running under enhanced controls; provisions already made, with only very minor further cost expected.
Cash deployment: acquisitions for capability gaps (small, like Heltar) and larger scale acquisitions under evaluation, plus internal optimisation and selective headcount; dividend program continues.
demand_pricing: Customer retention: net revenue retention 98% for the year; slight impact from one key customer, rest of portfolio described as stable.
Management says some aggregator accounts saw margin impact, recoverable through routing optimisation.
Competitive pricing aggression in WhatsApp and RCS; management says it will not chase price and aims to keep direct margins (DM) intact.
Delayed collections from several large customers in India and UAE in Q1 were described as timing/reconciliation issues, not defaults; management says no expected bad-debt issues.
Management sees RCS as the better-margin channel for aggregators and plans to promote it, including exclusive arrangements in certain geographies.
Truecaller partnership signed; testing with select enterprises, too early to size monetisation or margins.

qa_highlights.question: What is the cause of the sharp gross margin drop and when in the quarter did it happen?
qa_highlights.answer: A large Indian customer's traffic was disrupted during a last-minute development needed for a new solution; the company is in testing and expects partial recovery in Q1 and full recovery in the balance quarters. Management did not quantify the margin bridge, saying it would confirm the breakdown internally.

qa_highlights.question: Is the Masivian security incident a material margin hit?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the investigation is ongoing, impact assessment is in progress, and provisions have been made with only very minor further cost expected. Attestation is hoped for soon to win back affected enterprise business.

qa_highlights.question: Will gross margin revert to 22-22.5% or to the Q3/Q4 FY26 level of 24-25%?
qa_highlights.answer: Management declined to give a precise number for Q2; depending on recovery, the margin could land in the 21.5%-23% range seen over the last 5-6 quarters. Some items reverse automatically, others need routing work and take longer.

qa_highlights.question: Why has new product market share lagged competitors in WhatsApp and RCS, and are we losing share?
qa_highlights.answer: No published market share data exists. Management believes it has a decent share and says growth was deliberately limited to protect margins amid price aggression, so it did not chase low-priced volume.

qa_highlights.question: Will the non-SMS mix shift be margin accretive as it scales toward 20-30% of revenue?
qa_highlights.answer: Management would not commit to margin expansion or dilution from non-SMS products in FY27, citing varied regional margin profiles and different pricing models; Heltar targets higher-margin markets such as LATAM, Europe and the US.

qa_highlights.question: What is the timeline for Heltar to contribute meaningfully?
qa_highlights.answer: Scaling is expected to be gradual, as enterprise communication budgets do not shift within the same fiscal year; the company expects scaling to be visible by the last quarter of FY27 and to continue into FY28.

qa_highlights.question: Why was the India segment profit negative and what is the cash conversion outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: The negative India segment profit reflects the impacted large Indian customer. Q1 cash flow was weak due to delayed collections from large customers; management expects conversion to return to 75%-100% of EBITDA for the rest of the year.

risks_watch: Recovery of the disrupted high-margin Indian customer account and its traffic, expected in Q2 FY27.
Masivian/Colombia security incident: final impact assessment, regulator actions, and recovery of affected enterprise business.
Gross margin recovery toward the 21.5%-23% band; Q1 at 20.9% is below that range.
Adjusted EBITDA margin relative to the ~12% guidance referenced by analysts; management says it will have a clear view by end of Q2.
Competitive pricing pressure in WhatsApp/RCS and the new-product growth rate (14% YoY) versus peers, which management did not benchmark.
Cash conversion, with Q1 weak due to delayed collections from large India and UAE customers.
Claro deployment delays; revenue not yet flowing.
ILD growth stagnation tied to telecom operator pricing strategy.
Heltar closing and integration; no margin contribution guided for FY27.
summary.management_tone: Confident on the strategic direction and the new-product growth, but cautious and somewhat evasive on margins: management repeatedly called the drivers transient but gave no quantified margin bridge and declined to commit to FY27 margin or EBITDA numbers.
key_quotes: This is not revenue or gross margin that we have lost, but just a temporary disruption, which will be restored in the coming quarter as we continue to offer the new solution capabilities to these customers.
So that collection should flow in during the quarter and the collection -- the cash position for the rest of the year should go back to the typical 75% to 100% conversion from EBITDA
So for this year, we would not want to commit to any margin expansion or dilution because of these product solutions or the non-SMS product solutions.
Our attempts have been to grow the market without compromising on direct margins.

growth.why: FY27 revenue, margin and dividend guidance held with no update; management guided volumes up 10-15% over the next two quarters and gross margin of 21.5-23%, but backing is vague with no capacity, order-book or capex figures given beyond the Heltar acquisition, which is not capacity.
